title: Evaluate profiles
tagline: Project a chain onto a plane and cut it where it folds back -- or outline a part and split its outline into top, bottom and middle profiles.

slides.title: What it does
slides.problem: Side profiles of a core, a topsheet or a sidewall are needed as clean curves: for fills, for drawings, for measuring. Native Project and Outline give an undivided loop, with slivers, that can fold back at the tip. Evaluate profiles gives the profiles you actually want, named.
useWhen: You need a part's top / bottom / middle side profile
A projected chain folds back at a tip
An outline has micro-edges that break a fill
slides.caption: P1: a crowned sheet outlined: top, middle and bottom profiles.

points.head: Edges
points.body: Project, then cut where the chain stops advancing along the prevailing direction (400-sample scan, then bisection).

points.head: Part
points.body: The two longest runs along the direction are top and bottom (top = higher); the middle is their average at matching stations.

points.head: Micro-edges merged
points.body: Outline edges under 0.01 mm are merged away -- a 1.7 um edge once broke a fill.

slides.title: The dialog: Part
params: EDGES: project a chain. PART: outline a solid or surface.
Part outputs are named <name> top, <name> bottom, ...
A solid or surface body, or a face of one.
Top / Bottom / Middle / Periphery / All profiles / Full (profiles + connectors).
The direction profiles run along (+ flip). Default: the longest in-plane extent.
One curve / One per input curve (exact) / Efficient (merges exact lines and arcs; freeform only across tangent joints).
Scan, curve detail, colour the profiles.

slides.title: The dialog: Edges
params: One curve / One per input curve / Efficient -- see the examples.

slides.title: Example: One per input curve
slides.head: P10: lines 0-200-400 (collinear), a line to (700, 700), an R100 hook -- projected onto Top
slides.body: 4 exact edges: the projected edges themselves, the arc cut exactly where it turns back (at (759.55, 835.96)).

slides.title: Example: Efficient
slides.head: P11: the same chain, Efficient
slides.body: 3 edges: the two collinear lines merged into one 400 mm line; the slanted line and the R100 arc kept exact. One curve (P9) gives a single fitted spline instead.

items.head: Prefer exact output
items.body: One per input curve or Efficient keep lines and arcs exact; One curve is a fit.

items.head: Longest loop only
items.body: An outline with several loops keeps only the longest.

items.head: Efficient keeps corners
items.body: Freeform edges merge only across tangent joints (0.57 deg): a 28 deg corner stays a joint (P12), a tangent joint merges (P13).
